title: Bayes factor as a named marginal-likelihood ratio
dek: BF₁₀ = m(y|M1)/m(y|M0). Wikipedia model-odds update. Not Wilks' Λ, not a p-value.
story: A Bayes factor on Wikipedia is the ratio of marginal likelihoods, the number that updates prior model odds into posterior model odds. It integrates the likelihood against each model's prior, including over parameters you might have profiled in an LRT.
stats-lrt compares nested maxima. AIC/BIC penalise 2Δℓ. A Bayes factor is a third object. Mixing all three in one table without names is how TB genomics papers become unreadable.
Improper priors can make m(y) undefined. That is not a software bug; it is the math refusing the question.
deep: Lindley's paradox: large n can give a tiny p and a BF that still likes a sharp null, depending on the prior.
BIC is a rough Laplace approximation to a Bayes factor under specific priors — not the BF itself (stats-aic-bic).
Savage–Dickey is a density-ratio trick for nested nested parameters, not a licence to skip diagnostics.
Do not call a likelihood-ratio p-value a Bayes factor.

visual.caption: LRT uses two maxima. A Bayes factor uses two integrated likelihoods. Same pair of names, different functionals of the likelihood.
